standard_text: Discovery of electron, proton and neutron, atomic number, isotopes and isobars. Thomson's model and its limitations. key_sub: An orbital is set by n, l and m(l); it holds two electrons of opposite spin.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a tiny positive nucleus (protons and neutrons) with electrons around it. Bohr's model gives hydrogen energies En = −13.6/n² eV and radii 52.9 n² pm; a jump between levels gives a spectral line with 1/λ = RH(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²). Light and electrons have dual nature: E = hν and λ = h/mv.

Quantum numbers n, l, ml and ms describe each electron. A subshell has 2l + 1 orbitals and a shell holds 2n² electrons. Electrons fill orbitals by the Aufbau principle (lower n + l first), the Pauli principle and Hund's rule.

Example

n = 3, l = 2. Orbital?

l = 2 is d

Answer: 3d

Example

H, n = 3 → n = 2. Series?

lower level 2

Answer: Balmer

Common mistakes

  • Letting l equal n.
  • Filling 3d before 4s.
  • Forgetting the minus sign in En.
